_doc: Sand Creek Raceway through Lake Murray v4's engine (ledger 0078, Kevin 2026-11-03: "Lake Murray v4 should be what we build the rest from"). The PILOT: Sand Creek 0.35.0's line (OSM centrelines, its widths, its 3DEP profile, tracks/sand-creek/data) fed by tools/lm_engine_intake.py into the v021 loop assembler (tracks/san-diego-lake-murray/scripts-v021/blender/build_loop_blend.py), prepped / exported / spawned by engine-july (the snapshot in tracks/san-diego-lake-murray/engine-july-snapshot), gated by the same gates. Its own slug and install folder so it installs beside sand_creek_raceway. Every other key is Sand Creek's own (copied from tracks/sand-creek/track.config.json at 0.35.0); the assembler reads route.smooth_*, route.divided_double, terrain.terrain_band_m and scenery.* only.
name: Sand Creek Raceway (LM engine)
_osm_road_widths_doc: Real street circuit — after the project stage, scripts.gps.widths_from_osm map-matches each centerline vertex to its OSM way and sets curb-to-curb widths from lanes (arterials ~2x a side street) + writes intersection pads at the real junctions. Racetracks (defined widths) leave this off.

capture._doc: Sand Creek is a ROAD circuit stitched from real Commerce City streets, so its elevation is the REAL road-surface profile: USGS 3DEP sampled ALONG the real street centerline (3 m spacing), median-despiked + smoothed into a launch-free longitudinal grade, with the terrain conforming DOWN to that road. The phone's GPS/baro altitude is NOT used — it is too noisy on flat terrain and injected fake metre-scale bumps (56th/45th/Sand Creek Dr) and a phone-fell dip (~idx 1240); use_elevation=false ignores it. Captured TEXTURES and lateral evidence in realworld_capture.json ARE still consumed (do not delete the file). 'bridges' is RETAINED: evidence.level_bridge_decks uses it to hold a LEVEL deck (geometry only, no phone) over the two real Sand Creek crossings where bare-earth 3DEP dives into the creek bed — E 56th over Sand Creek (station ~2415 on the 0.33.0 OSM line, ~2485 on the old KML line; bare earth dips ~7 m) and Quebec over Sand Creek (station ~5887, was ~5950; ~6 m); both also get visual parapets/piers from build_env._creek_bridge. 'bridges' = [{center_m, len_m}] in lap-station metres. FRAMES (ledger 0068): level_bridge_decks reads center_m/len_m along the DRAFT line (centerline.local.json), drive_test, kn5_ground_check, build_mesh's lip exemption and tools/lidar_crossfall along the FINISHED line (data/finished_centerline.json), which is 14 m shorter by the E 56th bridge and 19 m by E 45th; the other two crossings were declared before that was known. An optional profile_m [[metres from the bridge's start (center_m - len_m / 2) along the finished line, absolute height in the 3DEP datum = y + origin elev_m], ...] lays a MEASURED deck on the finished line in place of the straight crest-to-crest grade (evidence.apply_deck_profiles), eased back to the road over profile_ramp_m at each end.

bridges.name: e56th_over_sand_creek
bridges._span_doc: 0.33.0 (ledger 0073): re-keyed by position onto the OSM line: the deck's start (2,404 m on the 0.31.1 finished line) is 2,356 m on the new finished line, so center_m = 2,356 + 59; len_m and profile_m unchanged (profile_m is metres from the start and absolute heights). The new line runs on 56th's OSM centreline, 2.9-3.2 m north of the old line (Google drove the eastbound lanes): the same deck, read along its median. On the OSM line the draft and finished stations differ by 3.8 m at this deck (14 m before). 0.32.0 (ledger 0068): the deck the 2020 source lidar classes as bridge deck (class 17), 2,404 to 2,522 m on the FINISHED line of 0.31.1 (source/lidar/e56th_bridge_deck.md); was center 2485 / len 100. Re-key after a line change: find the deck's start on the new finished line and set center_m = start + len_m / 2; profile_m moves with it. level_bridge_decks reads center_m/len_m on the DRAFT line, 14 m early here, which now only picks the bank-crest anchors of the approach grade (the west approach moved <= 1.1 cm); the deck itself is profile_m.
bridges._profile_doc: 0.32.0 (ledger 0068): [metres from the bridge's start (center_m - len_m / 2) along the finished line, absolute height in the 3DEP datum = y + origin elev_m]. -4 (2,400 m) and 121-126 (2,525-2,530 m): lidar ground medians of the approaches; 1-116 (2,405-2,520 m): the cubic fit to the class-17 deck medians (rms 0.9 cm), all from source/lidar/e56th_bridge_deck.md's recommended profile; 131-156 (2,535-2,560 m): the east approach, mean of the class-2 ground medians within 2.5 m (e56th_bridge_deck.json), which ran 0.13-0.23 m above the built road. The deck was held as one straight grade 0.41 m (median) under the measured deck, which is crowned 0.29 m; no step at either abutment (deck within 4 cm of the approach ground). The heights are the real road's and stay true on any line over the same deck.

road_text._doc: Big painted street-name decals at each turn-onto. mode 'along' = lengthwise down the lane (drive over it, head-tilt to read); 'across' = sign-flat facing the driver (wraps the road type to a 2nd line). cap_m = letter height across the road. flip_read/flip_up mirror the axes if it reads backwards in-game. min_leg_m = shortest street leg that gets a label.

crossfall._spans_doc: 0.33.0 (ledger 0073): re-keyed by position, 0.31.1's [2540, 2740] is [2491, 2690] on the OSM line's finished stations; the span now STARTS at 2540, just past the 56th slip's merge into Sand Creek Dr, because a Mac A/B showed the measured roll-in (+1.9 -> +5.1 % over 2,519-2,537) laid across the merge's 5.5 -> 23 m width flare made all 4 severe steps (2,529-2,532, 6.3-6.9 cm): starting at 2540 they are 0 (zeroing 2,515-2,545 only: also 0, but the camber rolls in, out and in again). The roll-in now reads +1.3 % at 2,529 to +4.1 % at 2,556, then 2.4 to 4.9 % through to 2,619. The whole-lap file (0.31.0) took kinks 11 -> 27 /km at the road edges and steps and drops on E 45th Ave (6,270-6,450 m), where the line likely rides the embankment, not the pavement. crossfall._doc: Ledger 0066, Kevin 2026-11-03 ("Yes, build it"): the road's real side-to-side tilt, measured off the 2020 USGS source lidar by tools/lidar_crossfall.py into data/crossfall.json (status measured), which build_mesh rolls every road section by. scripts.elevation.crossfall leaves a lidar file alone. Rerun the tool when the line moves: its cache data/crossfall.lidar.json is keyed to centerline.local.json.

source._doc: 0.33.0, ledger 0073 (Kevin 2026-11-03: the roads "are a bit wiggly w/r/t lines and curves/edges, they're not realistic and messy"; asked to re-source or only smooth Google's line: "Re-source from OSM"). The whole lap is real OSM street centrelines: route.roads names every way the lap drives, as 'id:' legs in lap order, fetched into data/osm.cache.json and stitched by scripts.gps.centerline.build_centerline; route.fillet rounds the polygon (scripts/gps/fillet.py). L1: KML only where a route leaves the road network, and this one never does (ledger 0070 A: every station of the old line is within 4.7 m of an OSM way).
source._history: Until 0.31.1 the line was Google Maps' Directions polyline, source/Sand Creek Raceway Drive-3.kml (source.type kml, 453 vertices ~14 m apart rounded to 1e-5 deg), resampled to 3 m: its vertices were the line's kinks (ledger 0070 A). The KML stays in source/ for history; no build step reads it. The ways were chosen by map-matching that KML onto OSM (ledger 0073 has the run table), so the streets and their order are the same lap.

route._roads_doc: Order = the lap, one leg per entry (build_ring joins each to the next at their shared node): (1) North Colorado Blvd, the northbound carriageway (oneway, the lap's direction) from E 48th Ave to E 50th Ave; (2) E 50th Ave; (3) N Ash St (the 50th Ave jog); (4) E 50th Ave to Dahlia; (5) Dahlia St north; (6) E 56th Ave east (one two-way way: its OSM line is the street's median line); (7) the 56th -> Sand Creek Dr slip, primary_link 628649529 (ledger 0066's camber corner); (8) Sand Creek Dr South; (9) N Northfield Quebec St, the southbound carriageway (oneway); (10) the Quebec -> E 45th slip, primary_link 944920188; (11) the I-70 frontage roads with their arrows: E 45th Ave, E 45th North Dr (incl. 944914475, a 6 m motorway_link piece of the same carriageway), E 46th Ave; (12) E 46th Ave Access; (13) E 48th Ave back to Colorado. Carriageways: where OSM has two one-way carriageways (Colorado, Quebec, the frontage pair) the lap takes the one it drives, never the median line between them: that is real pavement, the side whose lanes widths_from_osm reads, and the grid already drops the other side (route.grid.parallel_m). tools/route_oneway_check.py: no metre against an arrow.
route._start_at_doc: Station 0 = North Colorado Blvd northbound, 40 m north of the E 48th Ave node: the old KML's v0 was that corner itself; station 0 now sits on the straight just past the corner's arc, so the seam is on a straight (L13). The timing line and grids are layouts[].start, unchanged in place (re-keyed by position, ledger 0073).

fillet._doc: scripts/gps/fillet.py, before the 3 m resample. Each declared corner: the circle of radius_m tangent to both legs (radius_m = curb_radius_m + the mean of the two legs' half widths, half = scripts.gps.widths_from_osm.pavement_width / 2 of the way at the node: the width the ribbon is built at, so its inside edge follows a curb return of curb_radius_m). curb_radius_m [measured] read off NAIP 2023 (source/naip_2023_sc_z18.jpg, 0.46 m/px, about +-2 m): ledger 0073 has each corner's picture. Every other OSM node is rounded inside its own two segments after nodes within simplify_m (0.25 m [invented], under OSM's own accuracy) of their neighbours' chord are merged, so a curve OSM draws node by node keeps its own radius and a way join (the 56th slip merging into Sand Creek Dr at 26 deg) is not rounded inside one 3 m segment.

street_junctions._weld_hold_doc: ledger 0079 0.2.3 (coordinator 2026-11-05: the Y grid_tertiary_5 and the lens grid_tertiary_74 / 75 are real acute meetings, kept as acute welds): every acute mouth (the ones whose record carries extend_max_m) welds with tools/mouth_weld.py hold_overlap: its rows lie on the host deck (level across its edge) for the length its ribbon overlaps the host, from its first line's mitre to its last, and trim's 30 m ease starts only past that, instead of a 30 m smoothstep from each line's own mitre that left the overlapping rows off the host's level-across deck (round F: grid_unclassified_94 at 16.4 deg, 0.026-0.036 m over it). The length is the mitres' own, measured on the ribbon; no number is added
street_junctions._merge_forks_doc: ledger 0079 0.2.3 (coordinator 2026-11-05 under "I just want real": NAIP shows one asphalt with a painted chevron median, so build what's there): the two paint-divided approaches OSM draws as two one-way pieces leaving one node at 13-16 deg become ONE street (tools/trim_connectors.py merge_forks). edges_m [s, left, right] [measured]: the asphalt's two edges off NAIP 2023 (tracks/sand-creek/source/naip_2023_sc_z18.jpg, 0.46 m/px), read every 5 m on cross-sections sampled 0.5 m apart, each sample the mean over 1 m along the street; an edge = where the asphalt meets the first concrete band (curb, gutter, sidewalk) 1.5 m or wider (1 m bands inside are paint), in metres along the OSM midline's normal (-dz, dx) of the direction away from the fork node, s metres from the node; about +-0.5 m. Held past s 75: the curb returns into the lap there belong to the lap mouth. 91/92: 14.0 m at the node to 24.5 m at s 75; from about s 57 to the lap crosswalk a 3.5-4 m concrete island stands at +1 to +5 m (NAIP: bright like the sidewalks, so raised); it is NOT built, and the yellow chevrons s 20-55 are not painted: no chain step here makes an island or paints a chevron median on a grid street. 94/95: 13.5-14.5 m to s 55, 15.5 m at s 60-65, 18-19 m at s 70-75 (the flare into the lap); its median is flush yellow chevron paint, not painted here either. Round I (ledger 0079): 94/95 re-measured in the track frame (scripts.geometry.projection's WGS84 series; round G's helpers used 111,320 cos(lat) / 110,540 m and read both edges about 1.2 m west of where they are): the same cross-sections, the edge picked by rule = half-way to the first run of 3 samples (1.5 m) at NAIP gray >= 165 at least 4 m out from the midline (the rule reproduces round G's reads at 12 of 15 stations in round G's frame; 165 fitted to them [invented]); s 10's right edge has no such run (a car / driveway): interpolated between s 5 and 15. Both edges move +1.0..+1.5 m along the normal (east), width 13.5-15.5 m to s 70, 18 m at s 75. 91/92 moves 0.06 m in the right frame: kept.
street_junctions._median_crossings_doc: ledger 0079 0.2.3 (coordinator 2026-11-05: NAIP shows Quebec's median paved where 48th / grid_unclassified_27 crosses it at (1656, 789), so pave it): OSM ends grid_unclassified_27 at the west carriageway's node (1649.2, 789.4) and starts grid_tertiary_65 at the east one's (1662.7, 789.4); no way joins them, so the 4 m between the two carriageway ribbons stayed grass. tools/trim_connectors.py median_crossings adds the straight crossing node to node, kept at any length and welded at both ends. width_m 10.0 [rule]: grid_tertiary_65's own width, the wider of the two streets it joins, so its edges meet both (NAIP reads the cross street's west approach about 15 m curb to curb, centred about 4 m south of OSM's line: the streets' OSM widths are short here, a wider question than this crossing). Also measured: the strip between Quebec's two OSM carriageway ribbons (grid_primary_6 / 7, 4-6 m, narrowing to 1-2.5 m south) reads asphalt or concrete on NAIP at 48 of 49 samples along 860 m, never planted: owed to Kevin, not built here

No number

route._street_junctions_doc: ledger 0079 0.2.3 (Kevin 2026-11-05: "Real junctions"): tools/trim_connectors.py joins a street's OSM pieces where they end at one node and continue (turn <= join_turn_deg) or, two alone, bend (turn <= bend_turn_deg), then cuts every street-to-street meeting the lap and arterial passes did not: the through piece hosts, the other is cut at its pavement edge with a mouth (the ribbon-through topology every mouth here uses). Both angles [invented], but they sit in gaps of the data: Sand Creek's pairs turn 0-24 deg (straight) or 88-108 deg (bends) or 157-167 deg (forks), so any value in 25-87 / 109-156 makes the same joins (GATES-CHANGELOG 2026-11-05)
route._weld_exact_deck_doc: ledger 0079 round H (Lake Murray's ledger 0054 P1 key, opt-in): these mouths weld onto, and verify_mouths reads, the host deck off the host's own triangles: the lens grid_tertiary_74 on grid_tertiary_1#1 (HOST LANE 0.038 m), grid_residential_29#2 on grid_residential_22 (0.021 m), the crossroads grid_unclassified_10 on grid_tertiary_16 (0.065-0.084 m). grid_tertiary_16 there is not level across: lidar 0.11 m over its 9 m (20 m from grid_primary_33, whose grade its own mouth weld leans it onto; built 0.09 m). weld_exact_deck_lines (Sand Creek only): MOUTH LINE / NOTCH on those mouths read the host deck the same way (verify_mouths HDx; no tolerance moved)
route._weld_deck_beyond_end_doc: ledger 0079 round J (tools/weld_mouths_blend.py, mouth_weld.BeyondEndDeck): piece-name prefixes whose weld reads, past the host's OPEN end, the deck of the street that end is welded to. grid_tertiary_74#0 (24 deg) meets grid_tertiary_1#1 at its v1, where #1 starts on grid_tertiary_2#0: 74's first rows lie on grid_tertiary_2's pavement, and the host's end row held level there stood them 0.021 m over grid_tertiary_2's lane on its measured (lidar) profile, which falls 0.02 m over those 7 m (verify_mouths HOST LANE, grid_tertiary_1#1 start; round I's i3 / i5). Read off the street under them, they lie on it. No number added.
route._verify_mouths_allowed_doc: ledger 0079 round H (coordinator 2026-11-05: the 3 mouths at the parked pads stay allowed; do not work on the parked pads): tools/verify_mouths.py still measures each and marks its row FAIL, but these three named mouths do not fail the gate (a BYPASS, fleet/GATES-CHANGELOG.md). Every other mouth fails it as before; a name that matches no mouth is an input error. Remove a row when its pad is built
route._islands_doc: ledger 0079 round I (Kevin: "I just want real"): fork 91/92's concrete island, built where it was measured by tools/author_islands_blend.py after the weld, its heights read off the welded ROAD. rows [x_west, z, x_east, z]: NAIP 2023 (track frame) every 0.5 m from z -811.0 (the north nose) to -838.0 (the crosswalk's stop bar; through the crosswalk the refuge is cut flush, and the nose past it lies on the lap's own deck past the mouth line: neither built), each edge half-way to the first sample of the bright run (gray >= 185) covering x 53, samples 0.25 m; rows -835.0 / -835.5 (the run broken by a shadow, under 3 m wide) interpolated. x 50.88 .. 53.62-54.62 (3.75 m wide from z -817). rise_m [west, east]: lidar (CO_DRCOG_2_2020 class 2) median 0.25-1.25 m inside minus outside each edge, +-0.5 m along, over the 53 rows read: west +0.078 m (range +0.024 .. +0.216, the median taken: the spread is the lidar's, a curb is one height); east -0.047 m (-0.19 .. +0.05: the island at or under the northbound lane beside it, which rises east where the built road is level across): built flush, 0. Round H's single section at z -824 (0.4 m over the east carriageway) is the one row where the east lane dips; along the island it does not.

road_edge._doc: Urban street edge swept along every road: road -> raised curb -> flat sidewalk -> graded grass as ONE continuous profile sharing seam vertices with the road and the grass, so nothing hovers (scripts/geometry/ribbon.py:curb_sidewalk; physical 1KERB_sidewalk). Omit (or profile != 'sidewalk') for the default asphalt shoulder. curb_h/sidewalk_w/grade_w in metres.
road_edge._why: Kevin 2026-07-26: 'I do want sand creek to have no sidewalks so that's a valid build type'. Sand Creek is a RACING loop laid on real streets - the race-day overlay is concrete barriers along the line, not pedestrian furniture. Set profile back to 'sidewalk' to restore the urban edge.

scenery._doc: Per-track foliage/scatter knobs read by scripts/environment/build_env.py. Defaults (shown) reproduce the original look; override per track (e.g. a desert track wants sparser, lower scrub). corridor_margin_m keeps ALL scatter this far clear of every road (main loop + connectors).

streetlights._doc: Ledger 0070 D1, Kevin 2026-11-03: "same lamps as lake murray". The fixture is Lake Murray's current one (ledger 0056: tools/make_streetlight_led.py's led_cobra, two back-to-back arms, as Lake Murray's scenery.streetlights), stood by tools/author_lamps_blend.py (ship.json draft step lamps). planner engine_draft: the posts are planned by tools/plan_streetlights.py (draft step lamps_plan, after mesh) on the draft's own built surfaces — the loop's walk (every 55 m, alternating sides), the footprint off every road surface (the 1ROAD shoulder sheet included, so a post steps out past an embankment), >= 0.5 m + the mast radius from every wall, none on a deck span or a pad. Retired with this block (read only by scripts/environment/build_env.py, never a chain step): light_spacing_m 96, lamp_model street_lamp_new.obj, lamp_height_m 5.5, and the LIGHTPOST / LAMPHEAD texture_overrides (they would have re-skinned the LED pole with the old lamp's texture). The CSP light itself stays Sand Creek's own lighting.streetlight (Kevin's wide dim wash), not Lake Murray's 80s sodium.
streetlights._drop_on_road_doc: ledger 0079 round B: a draft post (the assembler's every-55 m rule) that a later road stands on is left out and recorded in lights.local.json dropped_on_road, never moved to an unmeasured spot (tools/author_lamps_blend.py)

signs._doc: Street-name blade signs at each major junction (from data/street_labels.json, same legs as the painted road decals). enabled=false drops them. flip_read/flip_up are one-bit fixes if the text reads mirrored or upside-down in-game (verify on the first Windows drive).

streetlight._doc: Kevin 2026-10-10: 'Can we do something about the lights? They're very harsh and very bright. And they need to be more like sodium lights from the 80s.' LOW-pressure sodium, not HPS: north of I-8 every City of San Diego street light was LPS from the Feb 1984 council vote (Palomar) until the 2002 broad-spectrum resolution, so Del Cerro's 80s lamps are the monochrome 589 nm yellow - color 255,165,30 (config is 0..1 floats, the writer scales x255) with single_frequency 0.9 as the sodium switch; HPS alternative if the hue reads wrong: color [1.0, 0.72, 0.30], single_frequency 0.7. 'Very bright' was a 255x scale error, not taste: CSP multiplies the 0..255 COLOR by intensity with no /255, so 1.6 was an effective 408 against a community median of ~10 (SRP 1.5); 0.01 = effective 2.55, the soft-sodium band. Ladder if too dark: 0.015 -> 0.02, ceiling 0.03, never back toward 0.1+. Harshness levers: SPOT 150 puts the cone rim (25.9 m at the 6.93 m light height) just outside the 24 m range edge so the gradient, not the cone, draws the pool; specular 0.6 -> 0.1 kills the asphalt glare; diffuse_concentration 0.25 + half-res blurred shadows soften the terminator and the black wedge under each post. emissive/emissive_color are inert here (LIGHTS_0_mat is the invisible 2 cm marker from the 2026-10-08 'glowing ball' fix, 5.0 -> 1.6 / 0.35 -> 0.08) but hue-matched for a future visible lens. Kevin 2026-10-11 after driving it: 'Lights need to be a bit brighter but not much' -> 0.010 -> 0.013 (+30%, under the planned 0.015 step); colour, cone and softness unchanged. Ledger 0056 (2026-10-14, the taller LED lamp: light 6.71 -> 11.43 m over the centreline, tools/streetlight_pool.py on CSP's documented range/spot/diffuse terms): UNDER each lamp the road stays in the RANGE_GRADIENT_OFFSET plateau (slant 11.4 m < 12.5 m) and the spot's full-strength core, so the brightness there is unchanged (+0.4 %); BETWEEN lamps the mid-block stays dark as before (3 % of midpoints lit, both) -> intensity stays 0.013, no scaling needed. What does change: the higher source puts the road 8-14 m from a lamp deeper in the cone, so the pool flanks are +16 % (quadratic fade) to +48 % (linear fade) brighter and the lit road +45-69 % on average, while the range sphere's ground footprint shrinks 24.0 -> ~22 m. If Kevin's seat reads that as brighter: 0.009 matches the road average (quadratic), 0.0077 (linear) - at the cost of the core under each lamp (-30-40 %); range_m 26.7 restores the 24 m footprint. 2026-10-14 (ledger 0056): with the taller LED lamps Kevin saw the preview and said 'They could be a little brighter' -> intensity 0.013 -> 0.015 (+15 %, the ladder's next step); seat-tune from here.

lm_pads._arms_doc: ledger 0079 0.2.3 (Kevin "authored pad junctions", "Real junctions"): tools/lm_pads_blend.py welds every street arm into its pad's deck. route.street_junctions.pad_arms cuts each street entering a built pad's box at the box edge (tools/trim_connectors.py cut_at_pads -> data/pad_arms.json); lm_pads splices that end row into the measured outline along the box edge, pins it as a seam and fades its departure from the lidar in (draft_pads.seam_offset_multi), and deletes only the lap's own faces between the cuts (within the lap's half width + its route.edge strip of the lap line). The rows go into pads.built.json rows (arm_rows names them), so verify_pads judges their seams
